{{Short description|American mathematician}}
'''Donald Steven Passman''' (born March 28, 1940, in New York City) is an American mathematician, specializing in [[ring theory]], [[group theory]], and [[Lie theory|Lie algebra theory]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Home Page - Donald S. Passman|website=Mathematics Department, University of Wisconsin-Madison|url=https://www.math.wisc.edu/~passman/}}</ref>

==Biography==
After attending the [[Bronx High School of Science]], Passman matriculated at the [[Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]], where he graduated with B.S. in 1960. He then became a graduate student in mathematics at Harvard University, where he graduated with M.A. in 1961 and Ph.D. in 1964.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|title=Donald S. Passman, Citation & Biographical Note|website=MAA Online News, Prizes and Awards, Mathematical Association of America, Deborah and Tepper Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|date=January 2000|url=https://www.maa.org/maa-online-news-and-features#haimo2cit}}</ref> His doctoral dissertation was written under the supervision of [[Richard Brauer]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=9144|name=Donald Steven Passman}}</ref> Passman was an assistant professor from 1964 to 1966 at the University of California, Los Angeles (U.C.L.A.) and from 1966 to 1969 at Yale University. At the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], he was from 1969 to 1971 an associate professor, from 1971 to 1995 a full professor, and from 1995 to 2011 the Richard Brauer Professor of Mathematics. In 2011 he retired as professor emeritus.<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Donald S. Passman: Curriculum Vitae|website=Department of Mathematics, University of Wisconsin-Madison|url=https://www.math.wisc.edu/~passman/vita.html}}</ref>

Passman has written 7 books<ref>{{cite web|title=Donald S. Passman: Publication list|website=Department of Mathematics, University of Wisconsin-Madison|url=https://www.math.wisc.edu/~passman/publist.html}}</ref> and more than 180 research publications.<ref name=bio/> He has given over 70 invited addresses, not only in North America but also in Europe, Brazil, Israel, and Turkey. He has been an editor for several mathematical journals, including the ''International Journal of Mathematics, Game Theory and Algebra'' (1991–2013), ''Beiträge zur Algebra und Geometrie'' (1993–2013), ''Algebras and Representation Theory'' (2001–2011), and the ''Journal of Algebra and its Applications'' (2001–2016).<ref name=CV/>

{{blockquote|His research interests include finite and infinite [[group (mathematics)|groups]], [[non-commutative ring theory|noncommutative ring theory]], [[group ring]]s and enveloping algebras of [[Lie algebra]]s.<ref name=bio/>}}

In 1963 Passman married Marjorie Mednick. They have two children, Barbara and Jonathan, and five grandchildren, Samuel, Rebecca, Abraham, Jordan and Eve.<ref name=bio/>

==Awards and honors==
* 1977 — [[Lester R. Ford Award]] for 1976 article ''What is a group ring?''<ref>{{cite web|title=''What is a Group Ring?'' by Donald S. Passman, Year of Award: 1977|website=Mathematical Association of America|url=https://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/what-is-a-group-ring}} (with link to PDF for article)</ref>
* 1989 — Plenary speaker, Canadian Math Society summer meeting, Windsor Ontario, June 1989
* 2000 — [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|Deborah and Franklin Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]], [[Mathematical Association of America]]<ref name=web>{{Cite web|url=https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|title=Recipients of the Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics; Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|access-date=2024-10-07|archive-date=2024-06-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608175318/https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 2005 — Conference, held June 10–12 2005 at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, in honor of Donald S. Passman<ref>{{cite book|editor=Chin, William|editor2=Osterburg, James|editor3=Quinn, Declan|title=Groups, Rings and Algebras: A Conference in Honor of Donald S. Passman, June 10-12, 2005, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, Madison, Wisconsin|series=Contemporary Mathematics, Volume 420|location=Providence, Rhode Island|publisher=American Mathematical Society|year=2006|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yaIbCAAAQBAJ|isbn=0-8218-3904-7}}</ref>
* 2012 — elected a 2013 Fellow of the American Mathematical Society

==Books==
* Permutation Groups, Benjamin, New York, (1968), [https://books.google.com/books/about/Permutation_Groups.html?id=_FK_UAqPIdQC pbk edition, Dover, Mineola, (2012)].
* Infinite Group Rings, Marcel Dekker, New York, (1971).
* The Algebraic Structure of Group Rings, Wiley-Interscience, New York (1977), [Krieger, Malabar, (1985)], [https://books.google.com/books/about/The_Algebraic_Structure_of_Group_Rings.html?id=2xrSHX-rpGMC pbk edition, Dover, Mineola, (2011)].<ref>{{cite web|author=Gouvêa, Fernando Q.|authorlink=Fernando Q. Gouvêa|title=Review of ''The Algebraic Structure of Group Rings''|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/the-algebraic-structure-of-group-rings}}</ref>
* Group rings, Crossed Products and Galois Theory, CBMS Conference Notes, AMS, Providence, 1986.
* Infinite Crossed Products, Academic Press, Boston, (1989),<ref name="Montgomery1991">{{cite journal|last1=Montgomery|first1=Susan|authorlink=Susan Montgomery|title=Book Review: ''Infinite crossed products''|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|volume=24|issue=2|year=1991|pages=391–403|issn=0273-0979|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1991-16044-1|doi-access=free}}</ref> [https://books.google.com/books/about/Infinite_Crossed_Products.html?id=p37CAgAAQBAJ pbk edition, Dover, Mineola, (2013)].
* A Course in Ring Theory, Wadsworth, Pacific Grove, (1991), [https://books.google.com/books/about/A_Course_in_Ring_Theory.html?id=OKvQDgAAQBAJ pbk edition, Chelsea-AMS, Providence, (2004)].
* Lectures on Linear Algebra, World Scientific, Singapore, (2022), [https://www.google.com/search?tbm=bks&q=lectures+on+linear+algebra]
